builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Context Compaction for World Models
summary: The technique replaces retraining or model-layer context-window expansion with an agent harness that compacts and selects prior world context for the world model. It adds harness complexity, compacted-state storage, and context-processing overhead without requiring foundation-model training. Retrieval can still fail if compaction omits state needed to reconstruct a revisited region, and sliding-window-attention models lose most of their context retrieval when dreaming.
rationale: The harness is compatible with constrained infrastructure and avoids retraining, but its retrieval benefit and failure modes require validation on the reader's world model and interaction patterns.

claims.statement: The technique replaces retraining or model-layer context-window expansion with an agent harness that compacts and selects prior world context for the world model. It adds harness complexity, compacted-state storage, and context-processing overhead without requiring foundation-model training. Retrieval can still fail if compaction omits state needed to reconstruct a revisited region, and sliding-window-attention models lose most of their context retrieval when dreaming.
Context compaction enables room retrieval up to 4 times beyond the world model's context window without retraining.
